text: In the bacterial CRISPR-Cas immune system, how is a 'memory' of a past viral infection physically recorded in the cell?
choices: A short 'spacer' sequence of the invader's DNA is integrated into the CRISPR array in the genome
The methylation state of the cell's chemoreceptors is altered
A stable depolarization of the membrane potential is maintained
Virus-specific antibodies are synthesized and stored
explanation: CRISPR-Cas records infections by having Cas1/Cas2 integrate a fragment of invader DNA as a new spacer in the genomic array; on re-infection the spacer is transcribed into a guide RNA that directs Cas cleavage of matching DNA. It is the most literal form of biological memory. Methylation (option 1) underlies chemotaxis adaptation, not immune memory; membrane potential (option 2) is bioelectric signaling; and bacteria do not make antibodies (option 3), which are a vertebrate adaptive-immune mechanism.
